questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I preferred an English-speaking country, and I have always wanted to visit Australia

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to manage everything, especially since we were the first group from our university on that exchange agreement, so there was no one to ask for advice. It all ended up working out really well, but I left before everything was finalized for my bachelor's project, which I have been writing during the exchange

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended a meeting at the school where I received help organizing my schedule (bachelor's project)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to find housing that is not very expensive. You are guaranteed housing options, but they don't promise anything about the price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I have lived really close to the school and shopping facilities, so I ended up finding something good, but it has been very expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All options are very expensive. (I have paid more than 8000 kr (DKK)  to share a room)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It can be a bit challenging to get everything sorted when registering from home.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You're assigned a coordinator who can assist, but it takes some time to get a response.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted, but it was troublesome, and initially I was assigned a schedule with clashes (overlapping hours).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to familiarize yourself with it from home, but don't stress if you leave without having everything completely under control. It's a very different school system, and schedules are typically sorted out during the first few weeks. (It's a very common issue for both international and domestic students.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My impression is that the classes are 'easier' than back home. But it's also a different system, and it takes a bit of time to figure out how they set up assignments, etc. However, the level allows you to travel and enjoy your exchange country while still keeping up with the coursework

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It reminded me a lot of what I know from UCPH - I've had lectures, practicals (labs), tutorials, workshops, etc

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CHEM3120: Environmental and Analytical Chemistry
PCOL3012: Drug Design and Development
And in addition, I was involved with a research group where I worked on my bachelor's project.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have spoken with a coordinator here about the possibility of opening up the option to take pharmacy courses for future exchange students. The courses I took while studying at USYD were not directly relevant, especially drug design and development, which were quite basic compared to the classes I usually take at home.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The kitchen was without utensils, etc., so I had to go out and buy plates, pots, etc. Similarly, I had to buy a duvet, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is really cheap. Groceries are slightly more expensive, but eating out is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of clubs and societies. In the first week, there is a welcome festival where all clubs and societies have a booth where you can come and learn about all the opportunities available.
There is a club for everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I have played squash and been part of a yoga society. 
I have also signed up for a surf camp. I can really recommend it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I have visited Tasmania during the mid-semester break (rented a car), explored Melbourne and Newcastle. There's also plenty to see around Sydney. I would also recommend visiting the Blue Mountains National Park (2 hours by train from Sydney). After the semester ends, I've booked a trip to Uluru and Cairns.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I don't think I've experienced any major cultural differences. Most of the cultural differences I've noticed have been due to meeting other exchange students from all over the world. However, I would say that Australian culture is quite similar to Western culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I have primarily met local students in my classes. For example, suggesting to grab a coffee together or meet up to work on assignments has been common. (I have mainly socialized with other exchange students outside of school). However, I have often been the only exchange student in my classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference might be that the city is more lively in the morning (rush hour at coffee shops is before work), and then it becomes quieter later in the day.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't think I've experienced any major cultural differences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a club or society and remember, Australia also gets cool during winter, so bring a jacket and a raincoat.

I would recommend opening a bank account—it's free for students. This way, you can avoid large fees, especially on your rent.
Order your Opal card quickly (half-price for students) (opal card = travel card)
It's much easier if you have an Australian phone number (you can easily buy a SIM card at Aldi)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: USYD is really good at hosting a lot of welcome events at the beginning, so you quickly meet a lot of friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It has been rewarding to experience that I can move to the other side of the world and build a daily life for myself. Additionally, I have practiced my English and am now more comfortable with it. It has also been rewarding to meet a lot of nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The hardest part was getting everything sorted with school and accommodation before I arrived

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I am so glad I took this opportunity to go on exchange, and I would really recommend it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
